size.note: Newman's 48–52 cm. Wikipedia gives length ~40–55 cm range depending on sex; wingspan quoted separately.

habitat: Hunts in hilly and open country, woodland and semi-desert; avoids dense forest. Local southern African breeders use montane cliffs (Cape/Namibia); Palearctic migrants range more widely in summer (Newman's; SABAP1).
summary: A small eagle of buzzard proportions with light and dark colour morphs. Pale morph (most common) has whitish underparts and a diagnostic white shoulder patch at rest; dark morph is largely dark brown. In flight a translucent wedge on the inner primaries is visible (Newman's).

similar.note: Wahlberg's is longer-winged with a longer square tail held mostly closed; lacks Booted's white shoulder patch and pale primary wedge (Newman's).
Kites have a forked tail; Booted's tail is not forked though upperwing can show a pale panel like a kite (Newman's).
Tawny is larger and bulkier; immature Booted can still look small-eagle-like (field guides).

research.note: Status is stored as summer-migrant. Kruger birds are mostly summer visitors from southern African breeders, with possible Palearctic birds, so neither palearctic-migrant nor intra-african-migrant alone fits. summer-migrant is the existing vocabulary for that. No seasonal plumage change is described in the sources consulted, except presence/absence of migrants. Gaps: No juvenile/immature image in selected set. No Kruger-labelled image in the selected set. Structured marks keep the common form. The dark form is not a separate variant. Dark morph entirely dark brown below; can be confused with other medium raptors (Newman's; SABAP1). The schema has no morph field. Colour phrases outside the vocabulary were stored as the nearest swatch: pale yellow to yellow.
